verdict.rationale: Quo ships its own public REST API with a published OpenAPI 3.1 spec, a versioning policy, and documented endpoints and MCP tools for calls, messages, contacts, transcripts and call summaries. That covers a real but limited slice of the product. The pack never claims API–UI parity. UI features such as custom ring orders, call transfers, phone menus, Sona setup, number provisioning and AI call tags have no evidenced API equivalents, and call summaries are plan-gated. Missing for 10: an explicit parity commitment or endpoint coverage for call routing, ring orders, phone menus, Sona configuration, number provisioning and AI call tags, and independent hands-on confirmation of breadth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Quo API enables developers to integrate powerful communication features directly into their applications and workflows.
Retrieve a detailed summary of a specific call identified by its unique call ID.
Search your contact list, look up a specific contact’s details, add new contacts, or update existing ones just by asking.
Pull message history from any Quo inbox, filter by contact, date, or topic, or list all your inboxes to see which numbers are available.
